title: Acts – Jude — The Early Church: The Twelve Apostles
summary: This lens pairs this stage with Genesis 12 – Malachi — Israel: The Twelve Tribes. Twelve tribes, then twelve apostles -- see that stage's note: this is a parallel this lens offers for testing, not a settled claim about how Israel and the Church relate.

title: Genesis 1–2 — Creation: God and Humanity in the Garden
summary:
This lens places this stage at the top of the ascending side, paired with Revelation 20–22 — The New Creation, at the bottom of the descending side. The pairing is this lens's own reading of the canon's shape, not a claim the text asserts about itself.
Read both passages side by side and judge the pairing for yourself.

title: Genesis 3–5 — The Serpent, the Exile, and the First Deaths
summary: This lens pairs this stage with Revelation 20 — Satan Bound and Judged. Genesis 3 narrates a serpent (3:1); it does not name it "Satan" -- that identification comes later in the canon (Revelation 12:9, 20:2), which is why Revelation 20's title can use the name and this one does not.

title: Genesis 6–9 — The World Judged and Destroyed
summary: This lens pairs this stage with Revelation 6–19 — The World Judged and Destroyed: both narrate God judging the world by a specific means, the flood here and a final judgment there.

title: Genesis 10–11 — The Nations and the Tower at Babel
summary:
This lens pairs this stage with Revelation 1–18 — Babylon and the Beast, reading Babel's scattering as an earlier instance of the empire-and-idolatry pattern Revelation pictures at Babylon -- one reading of the connection, not a claim either text states about the other.
Note that at Pentecost (Acts–Jude — The Early Church) the language division is pictured in reverse.

title: Genesis 12 – Malachi — Israel: The Twelve Tribes
summary: This lens pairs this stage with Acts–Jude — The Early Church. Twelve tribes, then twelve apostles -- this lens reads that as a parallel worth testing, not a settled claim about how Israel and the Church relate to each other; traditions disagree on that question (see Romans 9–11), and this lens does not adjudicate it.

title: The Gospels — Jesus Christ
summary: This lens places this stage at the mountain's peak: everything on the ascending side climbs toward it, everything on the descending side runs from it. That is a structural fact about how this lens is organized, not a claim about the Gospels' place in actual chronological history -- the Gospels are not the midpoint of the biblical timeline.

title: Revelation 1–18 — Babylon and the Beast
summary: This lens pairs this stage with Genesis 10–11 — The Nations and the Tower at Babel, reading the two as the same empire-and-idolatry pattern at an earlier and a later point -- one reading of the connection, not a claim either text states about the other.

title: Revelation 6–19 — The World Judged and Destroyed
summary: This lens pairs this stage with Genesis 6–9 — The World Judged and Destroyed: both narrate God judging the world, the flood there and a final judgment here.

title: Revelation 20 — Satan Bound and Judged
summary: This lens pairs this stage with Genesis 3–5 — The Serpent, the Exile, and the First Deaths. Revelation 20 is where the serpent of Genesis 3 is explicitly named "the devil and Satan" (20:2) and finally judged (20:10) -- this lens reads that as one of the clearest of its mirror pairings, since both the figure and the reversal are named in the text itself.

title: Revelation 20–22 — The New Creation: God and Humanity in the New Jerusalem
summary: This lens pairs this stage with Genesis 1–2 — Creation: God and Humanity in the Garden -- but this stage ends in a city, not a garden. Whether that counts as "more than recovered" is a reading this lens offers, not a claim the text states about itself.
